subject: NeuroQ security roadmap & architecture asks (post-demo)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@neuroq.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@neuroq.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: security & deployment items from today’s demo

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the immediate security/compliance items and the ask-list so your security team can triage. I’ve grouped by priority and included owners from our side for any clarifying work.

High priority (needed to complete procurement):
- SOC 2 evidence: you asked for a concise summary of our scope and Type II timeframe. Attaching the SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf). Rishi (me) will follow up with the SOC 2 narrative and auditor contact if helpful.
- Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned a short Excel-based vendor SQ. Please send the NeuroQ template (or we can start from yours) — Monica can fill the technical sections.
- Data residency & HIPAA/GDPR: you indicated U.S. data residency + HIPAA applicability for certain workloads. We need to confirm whether PHI will be sent to inference endpoints and whether you require Business Associate Agreement (BAA).

Architecture / deployment clarifications (design team asks):
- Network isolation: we covered both VPC peering + private link and an on-prem air-gapped option. To scope effort, we need a simple network diagram from your infra/security (ingress egress points, NAT, proxies). I’ve attached a template you can use (network-seg-diagram-template.vsdx).
- Egress controls & customer-managed KMS: you asked if keys can live in your HSM/KMS — short answer: yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployments.
- Model execution isolation: we’ll document the runtime isolation guarantees (single-tenant pools, KV cache per-tenant, no host-level shared volumes).

Next steps / owners: 
- NeuroQ security: send vendor SQ and a network diagram (owner: NeuroQ sec) — target: Tue 2027-06-01
- Redwood (Monica): initial vendor SQ draft / technical fill — target: Wed 2027-06-02
- Redwood (Rishi): SOC2 narrative + auditor contact and BAA draft if needed — target: Mon 2027-05-31
- Schedule follow-up call to review network diagram & controls — propose Tue 2027-06-03 10am PT

If helpful I can start the vendor SQ in parallel and route the technical answers back to you for review.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@neuroq.com>

Cc: security@neuroq.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: security & deployment items from today’s demo

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap. I’ve looped in our security mailbox (security@neuroq.com) and our infra lead Tom. A few clarifications from us to help prioritize:

1) SOC 2 / Attestation: we need the SOC 2 report (Type II) for vendor review. If you have a summary, that helps while we coordinate legal to receive the full report under NDA.

2) BAA: we handle PHI only in specific flows — we’ll map that per API use-case but likely will need a BAA if PHI is stored/processed.

3) Network diagram: attaching our vendor questionnaire in a follow-up email (Tom will send the filled template). For the diagram, we’d like to show firewall / outbound egress rules and whether any SSH/VPN ingress is required. If you prefer, Monica can mark up the template during the next call.

4) Air-gapped option: this is a harder ask for us. We’re exploring whether a fully air-gapped on-prem box is feasible (security will own feasibility). For now treat it as low priority but include rough estimate of what an air-gapped proof-of-concept would require (ops effort + additional security review).

We’ll aim to get the vendor SQ to you by Monday.

Best,
Samira
Director of Product
NeuroQ Health
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@neuroq.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@neuroq.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: security & deployment items from today’s demo

Hi all —

Quick technical notes / questions to help fill the vendor SQ and diagram: 

- PHI handling: if PHI will be transmitted, please indicate expected volume (avg API calls per day) and whether you expect to persist outputs. Our Private option can be configured so no persistent storage is used, or to encrypt output at rest using your KMS.

- Network egress: our Private deployment requires outbound TLS to our control plane only for telemetry by default; for air-gapped we can disable all external egress but that adds support overhead. Can you confirm if Telemetry/metric push is permitted to a NeuroQ endpoint instead?

- Ports & protocols: for VPC-based Private we rely on HTTPS (443) and optional gRPC over TLS. No SSH access is needed for the runtime; support access is via audited jump-hosts if approved.

- Diagram ask: please show your NAT/gateway and any proxy layers. If you publish a CIDR block for the cluster we can show required firewall allow-lists for the control-plane connections.

I’ll start filling the technical tabs in the vendor SQ as soon as we get the NeuroQ file. Vivek will own the KMS/HSM integration spec.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Rishi / team —

Per Samira: attached is our vendor SQ (neuroq_vendor_sq_filled.xlsx). The security team completed the non-technical sections and flagged the following must-haves:

- Proof of SOC 2 Type II or timeline to achieve Type II (legal needs dates).
- BAA language if we will be processing PHI (legal will review).
- Controls for key management and proof that your service can integrate with customer-managed KMS (if possible provide a short integration doc or checklist).

On air-gap: security flagged it as "possible but expensive." They asked for a rough effort estimate for a PoC (weeks of engineering + onsite/ops) — can you provide a one-paragraph estimate?

Also, we redacted some questions you might consider focused in the technical tab — look for cells with comments.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis

Tom / Samira —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and for sending the completed questionnaire. Quick replies to your asks:

1) SOC 2: attached summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf) includes scope and last audit period. We are completing a Type II for our Private-hosted production controls this quarter; I’ll send the auditor contact and expected completion date (target: 2027-08-15). Legal can take the SOC2 under NDA; I’ll coordinate a secure handoff.

2) BAA: we have a standard BAA template — I’ll circulate a draft by EOD Mon 2027-05-31 for your legal to review.

3) Customer-managed KMS / HSM: Vivek will produce a short integration checklist that shows the supported KMS providers and how keys are referenced from the Private runtime. Expect that by Tue 2027-06-01.

4) Air-gap PoC estimate (high level): for a constrained on-prem air-gap PoC we estimate ~4–6 engineer-weeks of effort (split infra + ops), one week of onsite coordination, and an increase in ongoing support costs due to restricted telemetry. Full quotation depends on your infra specs — we’ll refine after we see the network diagram.

Next steps I’ll take on: draft BAA, send SOC2 auditor contact, and draft a one-page KMS integration checklist (Vivek to review). Monica will start populating the tech tab in the vendor SQ.

Can we confirm Tue 2027-06-03 10am PT for the follow-up review call? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
